items.note: S1.3 gives the eight-row schedule on triples of [100], the map (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restoration of scratch wires for arbitrary initial values, matching Lemma lem:scalar-motifs. It omits that stage 2 runs the inverse schedule from Y to X, the gate definitions and neighbour rule, and the net-change argument (JV+RG)x=x, so nothing is derived.

S1.4 states the frame D_v per vertex, D_vD_u^{-1} per edge, commuting with pointwise gates, D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the per-route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, as at 793-825. It is an infer step with no derivation of the invariant.

The form x^T(I-J/9)y with <t_S,t_T>=|S cap T|-1, comparable labels, central 3->4 losses of h, L=Ich, the sum Wm-2N+2L by gate telescoping, and L_b/N=100/539 all match. The actual label construction (A, P, B, Q, the stage transitions and the gate-label table eq:motif-labels) and the residual table are missing, as is L_c/N and the binary orthonormal-basis argument.

S1.5.4 gives P_U at gates and sinks, -P_{U_a} at X_a, rank(P_V-P_U)=dim change, the N rank-one source exceptions, s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b and the deficit N-2L_b>0, as at 1156-1167. The endpoint identity I_m is asserted, but the plan never gives the sink labels (U_a^perp, F) from which P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m follows (1169-1171).

S2.1.1 states the proposition correctly (one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, s_c=W_cm-2N+2L_c<W_cm, C^{tensor m} on every role). The S2.1 method names weight additivity mod 4 and the Z/fourth-root endpoint fixes. It leaves out the Hadamard conversion of the character (-1)^{v.x} to X_v and the full-label/27-coordinate endpoint computation (1287-1310).

The plan gives L_b/N<1/2, deficit N-2L_b>0, s_c<W_cm, then the paper's step: relative deficit >20*2^{-50}, log m<20, m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-eta), so s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50} (1331-1344). The exact eta values and sigma=tau for the complex network are not written out.

S1.1 lists the elementary O(V) operations, including cyclic row splitting into W streams of volume V/W. S1.2 states the controlled shift y->y+a(controls) mod Q with the paper's two-block split at Q-a and opposite-order merge, plus rational-unit scaling.

The factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 is stated with the reversed-Bruhat remark. The shear method (triangular changes by controlled shifts, each one of Pi via D_j+=H_i, swap, D_j=H_i-D_j, giving exactly a interchanges) follows 1425-1446. The elimination proof of the factorization (1375-1391) and the choice of a prime q avoiding the denominators (1413-1423) are missing.

The plan follows the proof step by step: row split to W streams of volume V/W with row count divisible by W^{k-1}, frames Phi_M with endpoint I_m giving H<-H+D on every row, the three updates producing the interchange, s recursive calls, O(V) overhead including the fixed-tape parking schedule, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and the two-case unrolling.

The O(Vu^tau) bound, padding to [q^e], W^k row padding and base-m pieces with sum a_j m^{j tau}+O(V log 2e) match 1649-1734. The row field is described as rho high digits, but the paper joins the top rho digits of both chunks into a row field of range q^{2 rho} (1660-1680). There are no sub-steps.

P_M conjugation moves each C_{v_j} to a coordinate kernel, giving one C^{tensor f} child per residual vector on one slot. M is a fixed number of row additions, there are exactly s_c children, inverses come from (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, and H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. This matches 1849-1940.

The plan follows the paper's proof: the eight conditional updates (net effect, w restored, displacement at most four), guard set B with 10<=g<=2^{K-1}-11, the 80(f-1)2^{-K} union bound, T_0S_0^{-1} permuting B with repair by extraction and radix sort, and the normalized repair terms. The handling of the top position j_{f-1} by an elementary op is omitted (minor).

S2.3 (q_0=O(log d) chunks as row index, padded to a multiple of W^{k_0}, children of volume V/W) and S2.4 (F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), F(e)=O(e) for e<d^{1/2}, total O(d^{lambda'})) match. They are infer steps without the unrolling (internal sum O(e^lambda), leaves e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}, conditions on lambda').

The statement (Q_p(Hz), error <sqrt2 2^{-p}, O(Vd^{lambda'})) and proof route (phase frames, row split, packed basis changes, recurrence, exact guarded evaluation, row-sum-one disk bound) match. The guard width Delta=ceil(C_0 d^20)=o(p) is only asserted: its derivation by the depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E (2479-2560) is absent.

The plan covers character cancellation via the shift by t/2^{v+1} and no two-torsion, the DIF step, stored bit-reversed order B_tF_t^- with opposite F_t^+B_t^{-1}, layout L (O(dK) slot moves, at most Dq-1 chunk exchanges costing O(Tp pK^{tau-1})), one layer per round, and J_E commuting with Q_p for error sqrt2 ell 2^{-p}.
S3.4 states evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, four products with the established multiplier, centered-residue extraction justified by |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, and cost O(rp log(rp)), as at 3233-3265.

S3's method (two forwards kept in stored order, pointwise signed-packed products, opposite transform, exact scale by M) and S3.5's normalization F^-(f*g)=M(F^-f)(F^-g) with error total M(3 delta+eta) follow 3415-3473. The cost and error bounds match the proposition.

The plan uses the paper's route: Gaussian identity T P_sF_s=P_tF_tS, Neumann inversion of N=CTD, A=S/2, B_0=D'J'C with normalizations 2^{-2 alpha^2}, and the permutations kept rather than sorted (O(tp log t) saved). The tensor form RF_s=2^gamma B_0 QF_t A with gamma=2d alpha^2 and the axis-exposure cost are stated.

Both identities are stated correctly. S4.4 gives the paper's cancellation mechanism (F_s^+R=R^{-1}F_s^+, permutations commute with pointwise products). S4.3 omits the coefficient computation showing the chirp sum reproduces QF_t (3941-3951) and the periodicity of a.

The constants, sizes and prime intervals (1-2eta)t_i<s_i<=(1-eta)t_i are correct. So are the prime count exceeding d, Bernoulli giving T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta_i>3db>=p, the n^{o(1)} search and no wraparound with c_j<2^{3b}. These follow 4016-4193; eta=1/(4d) and the Rosser-Schoenfeld source are not named.

Isomorphism by the order-S argument, the triangular formula b_i=a_i+mu_i sum a_jP_j, prefix-controlled cyclic shifts of the valid interval in descending target order, padding preserved, and O(d^2) axis moves costing O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)) match 4216-4292.
S5.4 states the twist x_d->zeta y, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j and D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+f, iota D_+g)=(f*g)/T as at 4303-4341. The computed twist errors are not given.

The source transform composition (A, chirp via twisted ring convolution, B_0, exact 2^gamma) with exact counterpart RF_s, the conjugation for RF_s^+, and the pipeline with scalings by S and 2^{2b+4}S, rounding, Phi^{-1} and carries match 4456-4533. The input scale 2^{-b-2} is not mentioned.

E_ring=M(3L+2)<5TL, chirp <8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, the final bound 448b2^{-b+gamma}<=448b2^{-3b/4}<1/2 and the carry invariant are correct. The plan skips the pointwise-product and opposite-transform link ((2E_s+2), (3E_s+2), E_w=S(3E_s+2)<28*2^gamma T^2L, 4677-4709) and the use of gamma<=b/4.

The plan follows the paper's accounting. It normalizes by V=Tp, takes the minimum margin g_2=epsilon c(1-tau)=2^{-181}=2kappa from the layout chunk exchanges (O(p/K) exchanges, cost O(pK^{tau-1})), and treats exceptional sorting as O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})=o(V). It absorbs log powers in p^kappa and uses a schoolbook cutoff. The individual table rows are only summarized.
S0 concludes that the O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) machine means no eventual Omega(n log n) lower bound holds in this model, which agrees with 381-387. It does not spell out the liminf formulation.

errors.says: The layout lets every transform round be one simultaneous layer plus a record monomial.
errors.paper: Only rounds on the chunked part use the simultaneous layer; rounds on the prefix slots are processed bit by bit with individual butterflies (the dK term).

errors.says: Take rho=O(log e) high digits as a row field padded to a multiple of W^k.
errors.paper: The top rho digits of each chunk are interchanged and joined, so the row field is (d^+,h^+) with range R=q^{2 rho}>=W^k before both remaining chunks; this is later undone.

chain: The tree reaches the main bound by the paper's route. Two power-saving primitives come first: the bit network with labels, ranks and the shear recurrence giving O(Ve^tau), and the complex network with phase frames, packed bit additions and the layer recurrence giving O(Vd^{lambda'}). Then come synthetic transforms and convolution, resampling with retained permutations, the chirp and cancellation, assembly, exact recovery and cost accounting. It thins out in a few places: the explicit label construction behind Lemma lem:motif-residuals, the guard-width depth recurrence, the elimination proof of the triangular factorization, and the E_w link in the error chain. These are asserted, not shown.

steps.note: S1.3 gives the fixed linear network on three-element subsets of [100] sending (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restoring every scratch wire. N is named as the number of data pairs and m as the dimension of F^{tensor 3}, but the closed forms N=C(100,3)^3, m=h^3 are only implicit.
S1.4 states the common frame commuting with pointwise gates, the implemented operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the per-route operator, as at 812-822.

The plan has nondegenerate tensor labels in F^{tensor 3} built from triple indicators (S1.5.1 form), every edge joining comparable labels, and the only decreases at central wires from time 3 to 4, each losing h=100. The explicit gate-label table is not reproduced.
S1.5.4: edge matrix rank equals dimension change, except the N first source edges of rank one where the dimension change is zero.
S1.5.2 gives L=Ich and sum |Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L via gate telescoping. S1.5.4 gives s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b.
L_b/N=100/539<1/2 and deficit N-2L_b>0, so s_b<W_bm. The complex ratio 101/539 is not given, but the bit chain is complete.
Endpoint difference I_m on every role (S1.5.4) and f'_{rho(w)}=Phi_{I_m}f_w giving H<-H+D on every row including scratch rows (S1.6.2). The sink-label computation behind I_m is not shown.
A=E_1 Pi E_2, a rank-a shear done with exactly a interchanges plus O(V) triangular work, and recursive calls totaling s per node.
Children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50} from the deficit exceeding 20*2^{-50} and log m<20. Unrolling gives F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the whole chain of the central saving: the fixed bank-exchange network, frames, nested labels with central losses of h, rank equal to dimension change plus N rank-one source edges, the budget s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b, the strict deficit from L_b/N=100/539, the endpoint identity giving the shear, edges as rank-many recursive interchanges, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. Its thinnest points are that N and m appear only implicitly and that the explicit label table and sink-label computation are asserted rather than shown.
